muse-code+muse-spark-1.3@xhigh.answer:
The fish partially visible at the very top-right edge of the image, cut off by the right frame, is swimming toward the left of the tank and away from the surface.

The visible portion shows the head with the eye and pointed snout facing left and slightly down, while the body curves up and to the right where it exits the frame. Because fish swim head-first, the head direction indicates travel toward the left side of the tank.

The long axis of the body is angled downward to the left: the rear of the visible body is higher, nearer the top-right, and the head is lower. That downward-left heading means the fish is swimming away from the surface, which is at the top of the image, not toward it and not level with it.
